input.quote: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.
input.rationale: Section 7(a) caps both parties, so mutuality is satisfied, and 7(b) excludes indirect/consequential damages mutually. However, the cap fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) the basis is total fees paid for the relevant Services rather than 12 months' fees, so for a short or front-loaded engagement Contractor's exposure can fall well below six months' fees; and (ii) there are no carve-outs at all — the only exception points to "PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF", which in this document is the Independent Contractor clause (there is no indemnification section anywhere in the Agreement), so the carve-out is a dangling reference and indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct all sit inside the cap. We therefore target the fallback: both caps set at fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim, with mutual Excluded Claims for indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct. We have not pressed the preferred USD 1,000,000 floor or the additional data-protection, fraud, IP and payment-obligation carve-outs.

This is our fallback liability position.
